bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- We are among the leading global manufacturers of machinery and equipment for technical textiles by revenue in 2024, with a strong focus on solutions for producing PP and HDPE woven fabric and sacks (“Raffia”). (Source: F&S Report, page 193) In 2024, we ranked among the top global players by revenue, with a 15.4% share of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value. (Source: F&S Report, page 193).
- We derive a significant portion of our revenue from operations from the manufacture and supply of machines for woven fabric and sacks.
- The demand for the machinery and equipment we manufacture is dependent on the demand for the end-use products, which have packaging and non-packaging applications such as agriculture, horticulture, fisheries, and forestry textiles, architectural and constructional textiles, clothing textiles and geotextiles.
- The cyclical nature of the agriculture, textiles and construction industries, both globally and in India, means that the demand for machinery and equipment for manufacturing technical textile may vary. (Source: F&S Report, page 188) Our sales volumes, profitability and liquidity are closely tied to the level of agricultural, construction and textiles activity worldwide, as the end-users for our products primarily operate in the agriculture, constructions and textiles sectors and are, therefore, affected by factors that affect these sectors, including the levels of investment and production in these specific sectors of the global and domestic economies.
- In particular, the agricultural sector is inherently seasonal and is further impacted by factors including agricultural commodity prices, costs of fertilizers and adverse weather conditions. (Source: F&S Report, page 188) Similarly, the construction sector is prone to seasonality owing to factors such as the inconsistent real estate market, economic downturns that cease construction activity, among others.
- For instance, such regulations may impose conditions on the quality of products our machines manufacture, which may require us to modify our product offerings, or provide mandatory requirement for usage of certain materials in packaging materials, and which may negatively affect the demand for and the valuation of our products.
- Any changes in government policy on the use of plastic for packaging, particularly in sectors in which our customers operate, may lead to variation in demand for our products.
- Significant increases or fluctuations in prices of, or shortages of, or delay or disruption in supply of primary raw materials could affect our estimated costs, expenditures and timelines which may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

business.body: We manufacture a comprehensive and diverse suite of machinery such as tape extrusion lines, circular loom, coating and lamination lines, printing machines, conversion machines, multifilament yarn machines, twister winders, monofilament extrusion lines and recycling machines, amongst others, as well as spare parts. We provide end-to-end solutions for the entire ecosystem of woven fabric, offering services from ‘concept to commissioning’, throughout the complete production lifecycle required for the Raffia industry. We manufacture winders and rewinders for high performance fibres and we have also ventured into extrusion lines to produce technical monofilaments with diversified applications such as textiles, agriculture and sports.

- Lohia Trade Services Limited (formerly Lohia Corp Limited) — Demerged Company: Its technical textile machinery business undertaking, including investment in five subsidiaries, was demerged into the Company under the Scheme approved by NCLT Allahabad on April 16, 2024; appointed date April 1, 2024, effective date May 1, 2024.
- Leesona Corp — Subsidiary (USA): In 2019 the business and assets of Leesona Corp were acquired through LC Acquisition, Inc., a subsidiary of the Demerged Company, which was renamed Leesona Corp. after the acquisition; brought winding technology and machinery for high performance fibres.
- Sundarlam Industries Private Limited — Group entity incorporated following a 2021 acquisition: In 2021 the Demerged Company acquired the lamination/coating machines business for woven fabric from a company in Bengaluru and incorporated Sundarlam Industries Private Limited.
- J.J. Jenkins Inc — Business acquired in 2024 through Subsidiary Leesona Corp: Supplier of synthetic fibre and monofilament machinery in the United States; acquired to expand the specialty yarns and tapes portfolio for medical and defence applications.
- OMGM SAS — Shareholders' agreement counterparty (manufacturer in Italy): Company has commenced sale of extrusion lines for technical monofilaments and for production of straps and ropes pursuant to this agreement.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: We manufacture a comprehensive and diverse suite of machinery such as tape extrusion lines, circular loom, coating and lamination lines, printing machines, conversion machines, multifilament yarn machines, twister winders, monofilament extrusion lines and recycling machines, amongst others, as well as spare parts. We provide end-to-end solutions for the entire ecosystem of woven fabric, offering services from ‘concept to commissioning’, throughout the complete production lifecycle required for the Raffia industry. We manufacture winders and rewinders for high performance fibres and we have also ventured into extrusion lines to produce technical monofilaments with diversified applications such as textiles, agriculture and sports.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Lohia Trade Services Limited (formerly Lohia Corp Limited) — Demerged Company: Its technical textile machinery business undertaking, including investment in five subsidiaries, was demerged into the Company under the Scheme approved by NCLT Allahabad on April 16, 2024; appointed date April 1, 2024, effective date May 1, 2024.
- Leesona Corp — Subsidiary (USA): In 2019 the business and assets of Leesona Corp were acquired through LC Acquisition, Inc., a subsidiary of the Demerged Company, which was renamed Leesona Corp. after the acquisition; brought winding technology and machinery for high performance fibres.
- Sundarlam Industries Private Limited — Group entity incorporated following a 2021 acquisition: In 2021 the Demerged Company acquired the lamination/coating machines business for woven fabric from a company in Bengaluru and incorporated Sundarlam Industries Private Limited.
- J.J. Jenkins Inc — Business acquired in 2024 through Subsidiary Leesona Corp: Supplier of synthetic fibre and monofilament machinery in the United States; acquired to expand the specialty yarns and tapes portfolio for medical and defence applications.
- OMGM SAS — Shareholders' agreement counterparty (manufacturer in Italy): Company has commenced sale of extrusion lines for technical monofilaments and for production of straps and ropes pursuant to this agreement.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- We are among the leading global manufacturers of machinery and equipment for technical textiles by revenue in 2024, with a strong focus on solutions for producing PP and HDPE woven fabric and sacks (“Raffia”). (Source: F&S Report, page 193) In 2024, we ranked among the top global players by revenue, with a 15.4% share of the global woven Raffia machinery market by value. (Source: F&S Report, page 193).
- We derive a significant portion of our revenue from operations from the manufacture and supply of machines for woven fabric and sacks.
- The demand for the machinery and equipment we manufacture is dependent on the demand for the end-use products, which have packaging and non-packaging applications such as agriculture, horticulture, fisheries, and forestry textiles, architectural and constructional textiles, clothing textiles and geotextiles.
- The cyclical nature of the agriculture, textiles and construction industries, both globally and in India, means that the demand for machinery and equipment for manufacturing technical textile may vary. (Source: F&S Report, page 188) Our sales volumes, profitability and liquidity are closely tied to the level of agricultural, construction and textiles activity worldwide, as the end-users for our products primarily operate in the agriculture, constructions and textiles sectors and are, therefore, affected by factors that affect these sectors, including the levels of investment and production in these specific sectors of the global and domestic economies.
- In particular, the agricultural sector is inherently seasonal and is further impacted by factors including agricultural commodity prices, costs of fertilizers and adverse weather conditions. (Source: F&S Report, page 188) Similarly, the construction sector is prone to seasonality owing to factors such as the inconsistent real estate market, economic downturns that cease construction activity, among others.
- For instance, such regulations may impose conditions on the quality of products our machines manufacture, which may require us to modify our product offerings, or provide mandatory requirement for usage of certain materials in packaging materials, and which may negatively affect the demand for and the valuation of our products.
- Any changes in government policy on the use of plastic for packaging, particularly in sectors in which our customers operate, may lead to variation in demand for our products.
- Significant increases or fluctuations in prices of, or shortages of, or delay or disruption in supply of primary raw materials could affect our estimated costs, expenditures and timelines which may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
